body.claim: Ranking is corrections, then the share of commits that were corrective, then authors, then commits — and a range with a single commit is given a share of zero.
body.detail: A range corrected twice in four commits is a range that keeps going wrong. A range corrected twice in twenty is usually one everybody has to edit, like the enum a new subcommand is added to, and it should not head the list. One commit is not a rate, so a single corrective commit scores no share at all: it is still evidence, but it must not outrank a range corrected repeatedly.
